advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Have check_auth assert the response is a 2xx that returns the expected self-account JSON (not merely that no exception was raised) so a redirect-to-login cannot read as authenticated.
evidence: src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py:132-134: `check_auth` calls `self._request("GET", "/a/accounts/self", timeout=5)` and only raises via _request's HTTPError/URLError paths.
gerrit_client.py:122: `with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:` — default opener follows redirects, so a 3xx→200 login page is not a GerritError.
check_auth never inspects the response body or asserts it is the expected account JSON, so 'checked and authed' is indistinguishable from 'redirected to an anonymous 200'.
advisory.finding: check_auth treats any non-raising _request as authenticated success, but urllib.request.urlopen follows 3xx redirects by default; a Gerrit misconfiguration that redirects /a/accounts/self to an anonymous login page returning 200 would pass check_auth even though the bot is NOT authenticated — the auth oracle can report 'authed' when it never truly verified identity.
scenarios: Gerrit fronted by an SSO proxy that 302s unauthenticated /a/ requests to a login page returning 200
advisory.suggested_fix: Have check_auth capture (status, text) and verify status==200 and that _strip_xssi(text) parses to an object containing the bot's account id, rather than trusting the absence of an exception.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Do not couple the autodeploy post-deploy gate / rollback to Gerrit auth: keep /health liveness-only or move the auth check to a separate readiness route that curl -fsS does not gate on.
evidence: src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:549 `response.status_code = 503`

infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:1052 `while ... curl -fsS -m 3 "$HEALTH_URL" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { ok=1; break; }`
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:1056-1057 `err bot-unhealthy "...ROLLING BACK to :prev..."; if [ "$have_prev" = 1 ]; then docker tag "$BOT_IMAGE:prev" "$BOT_IMAGE:latest"...`
app.py:514 docstring: `Liveness probe ... (no kernel call).`
src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:541 `auth_ok, auth_reason = await asyncio.to_thread(_gerrit_auth_health, app.state.config)`
src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py:134 `self._request("GET", "/a/accounts/self", timeout=5)`
infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:451 `# Auth ON at /mcp (static bearer). /health stays unauthenticated (custom route).`
infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:325-327 healthcheck `interval: 30s`
infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:65 external `GET /review/health` reaches app as `GET /health`
advisory.finding: Adding a Gerrit auth check that returns 503 to /health couples the review-bot's autodeploy post-deploy health gate to an external dependency; `curl -fsS` treats 503 as failure, so a Gerrit auth outage or expired/rotated bot token causes every newly deployed container to fail its health check and auto-ROLLBACK to :prev, making the service undeployable during an auth incident (widened blast radius).
merged_from: The /health route now performs an outbound authenticated HTTP call to Gerrit (/a/accounts/self) on every probe, and compose annotates /health as unauthenticated and auth-independent; this puts the bot HTTP token on a high-frequency, publicly-reachable-through-nginx route and generates a Gerrit auth request on each docker (30s) + host + autodeploy probe.
scenarios: Gerrit unreachable or bot HTTP token expired during a review-bot deploy → new container never returns 200 → automatic rollback loop
Token rotation lands before Gerrit propagates → deploy blocked
advisory.suggested_fix: Expose the Gerrit-auth check on a distinct endpoint (e.g. /readyz) and leave /health as pure liveness returning 200, OR make autodeploy's post-deploy gate tolerant of 503 (accept 200/503 and read the body) so an auth outage does not trigger rollback.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Keep the compose HEALTHCHECK bound to liveness only; do not let a Gerrit auth failure mark a live, draining container unhealthy.
evidence: infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:324 `test: ["CMD", "python", "-c", "import urllib.request,sys; sys.exit(0 if urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/health', timeout=4).status==200 else 1)"]`
src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:549 `response.status_code = 503`
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:338-343 health status `unhealthy`/`healthy`/none → `wedged`
advisory.finding: The docker-compose HEALTHCHECK asserts `.status==200`, so the new 503-on-auth-failure behavior will flip a running review-bot container to docker `unhealthy` whenever Gerrit auth is unavailable, even though the process is alive and draining — and autodeploy's bot_unreachable_disposition reads that health status to decide redeploying-vs-wedged, so an auth outage can be misclassified as `wedged`.
scenarios: Gerrit auth fails on a live bot → container flips unhealthy after 3 retries → alarms/ops treat a healthy process as dead
advisory.suggested_fix: Point liveness (compose HEALTHCHECK) at a route that stays 200 while the process is alive; report Gerrit auth on a separate readiness/metrics path.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile /health returning 503 on Gerrit auth loss with autodeploy's `curl -fsS` post-deploy liveness gate (autodeploy.sh:1052) so a transient Gerrit failure cannot roll back a healthy process.
evidence: src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:549: `response.status_code = 503`
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:1050-1052: `# END-TO-END health check (liveness: process up + /health 200).` ... `curl -fsS -m 3 "$HEALTH_URL" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { ok=1; break; }`
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:1056: `err bot-unhealthy "review-bot failed health check within ${HEALTH_TIMEOUT}s after deploy; ROLLING BACK to :prev ..."`
The health docstring bills the route as a liveness probe (app.py:514 `Liveness probe`), and the deploy gate treats it as liveness-only.
infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:324: `test: ["CMD", "python", "-c", "import urllib.request,sys; sys.exit(0 if urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/health', timeout=4).status==200 else 1)"]`
src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:549: `response.status_code = 503` (urlopen raises HTTPError on 503, yielding a non-zero exit in the probe)
GerritClient.check_auth uses a 5s timeout (gerrit_client.py:134) while the healthcheck `timeout: 5s` (docker-compose.yml:326) leaves essentially no margin for the extra Gerrit round-trip.
src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:552: degraded body still includes `"in_flight": _voter.in_flight_reviews()`
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:307: `body="$(curl -fsS -m "$INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT" "$HEALTH_URL" 2>/dev/null)" || { echo -1; return 0; }`
autodeploy.sh:302-304 documents that -1 is treated as fail-OPEN by the drain gate.
blocking.finding: Adding a Gerrit auth check to /health that returns 503 breaks the autodeploy post-deploy liveness gate: `curl -fsS "$HEALTH_URL"` fails (non-zero) on HTTP 503, so a bot deployed while Gerrit auth is transiently missing/rejected fails the health gate and is automatically ROLLED BACK to :prev, even though the process is fully up.
merged_from: The container HEALTHCHECK hits /health and marks the container unhealthy on status != 200 (or when urlopen raises HTTPError on 503), so a transient Gerrit auth/reachability problem now flaps the review-bot container into `unhealthy` even though the process, queue, and in-flight tracking are fully functional.

A degraded (503) /health response still contains a valid `in_flight` field, but autodeploy's `bot_in_flight_reviews` reads it with `curl -fsS`, which aborts on 503 and echoes -1 ('unreachable'), so the drain gate loses the real in-flight count during auth degradation and can recreate the container while a review is genuinely in flight.
scenarios: Gerrit restarting/rotating credentials during a review-bot deploy tick
Bot deployed before its Gerrit service-account token is provisioned

infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:324: `test: ["CMD", "python", "-c", "import urllib.request,sys; sys.exit(0 if urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/health', timeout=4).status==200 else 1)"]` — urlopen raises HTTPError on 503, so the healthcheck exits non-zero → unhealthy
Previously /health always returned 200 ({"status":"ok",...}) regardless of gerrit auth, so this healthcheck was purely a liveness probe.

infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:1056: `err bot-unhealthy "review-bot failed health check within ${HEALTH_TIMEOUT}s after deploy; ROLLING BACK to :prev ..."`
autodeploy.sh:1050 comment: `# END-TO-END health check (liveness: process up + /health 200).` — the gate is documented as a 200 liveness check, now no longer guaranteed 200
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:307: `body="$(curl -fsS -m "$INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT" "$HEALTH_URL" 2>/dev/null)" || { echo -1; return 0; }` — `-f` returns error on 503, so body is unset and it echoes -1
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:302 comment: `# How many reviews the review-bot is running RIGHT NOW, from its /health in_flight field.`
The new degraded branch still emits in_flight in the body (app.py) but the 503 status prevents curl -fsS from ever reading it, so the field is present yet unreachable to this consumer.
blocking.finding: The /health endpoint now returns HTTP 503 when the Gerrit bot credential is missing/rejected, but the docker-compose healthcheck asserts `status==200` — so a running bot whose gerrit token is rejected now flips the container to `unhealthy`, a new behavior for a process that is up and serving.
merged_from: autodeploy.sh's post-deploy end-to-end health gate uses `curl -fsS` which fails on HTTP 5xx; the new /health 503-on-gerrit-auth-loss will fail that gate and trigger a rollback to :prev for a freshly deployed bot whose only fault is a missing/rejected gerrit token.

autodeploy.sh's drain gate reads `in_flight` via `curl -fsS` (fails on 5xx); a /health 503 makes the body empty so bot_in_flight_reviews() returns -1 (unknown), silently changing the drain decision for an auth-degraded bot that is still processing reviews.
